A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same overlap-decomposition research, despite the title changing from Relative to Quotient Homology. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D support reliable comparison across the reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original nonlinear-curve simulations, its own reproduction of Naitzat et al.'s experiments, and measurements of sphere-classification networks before and after training, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds MNIST polyhedron-occupancy measurements and computational timing experiments in Appendix D.

M1.justification: v1's distance-threshold alternative in Section 3.1.1 and Algorithm 1 is removed. The principal linear-programming, union-find, and quotient-metric computation remains. The coarser-decomposition definition and revised pseudocode clarify the existing procedure rather than establish a new implementation.

E1.justification: v3 extends the previously synthetic coverage to MNIST image classification. Figure 6 analyzes polyhedron occupancy in four-layer networks trained and evaluated on all 60,000 digits. The nonlinear curves, Naitzat datasets, and concentric-sphere tasks remain.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain standard persistent homology for nonlinear curves and the reproduced Naitzat et al. pipeline for layerwise topology. Newly cited TDA methods are not added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: New diagnostic protocols include MNIST widths of 10, 25, 50, 75, and 100, and timing two-layer networks on 1,000 sphere-derived points while varying width, input dimension, and sensitivity. The original experiments retain the settings in Tables 1–3, including splits, training budgets, neighborhood parameters, and distance cutoffs.

E4.justification: New Figure 6 examines width-dependent polyhedron occupancy as indirect evidence concerning the convexity assumption. New Figure 7 measures computational scaling and sensitivity of runtime to the distance cutoff. These add substantial assumption and feasibility diagnostics; existing rank checks, curve-error examples, orthogonal-initialization comparisons, and expressivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: Figure 2 now clips the proposed method's upper shaded error bands at 9 and explicitly discloses this practice; v1's bands could exceed 9. Existing model counts, mean-and-standard-deviation summaries, and Bonferroni-corrected Kruskal–Wallis tests remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v3 adds MNIST occupancy and performance results, including reported performance of 0.913 at width 10 and 0.989 at width 100, plus runtime results across dimensions, widths, and cutoffs. These broaden the empirical findings beyond the retained curve examples, central Betti-number curves, and training/initialization comparisons; they do not establish a same-setting performance gain over v1.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.2 and Appendix B replace relative-homology expressions with quotient-homology statements. Theorem B.2 revises the rank/overlap union identity using containment and a pairwise-intersection operation. Appendix B adds the coarser decomposition in Equation 7 and a homotopy argument, while Appendix A.5 adds sequential relative-homology sequences connecting multiple identifications to quotient homology. These are substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The claims about separating topology from geometry, slower topological simplification, and training-dependent overlap structure remain. The abstract and contribution list refine the central assertion from relative to quotient homology and narrow the advertised overlap-detection approaches to linear programming.

C2.justification: v3 interprets decreasing MNIST occupancy as support for the convexity assumption and explicitly discusses faster computation versus potentially missed topology at small sensitivity values. Section 4.3 also corrects the classification rationale from more injective to more non-injective. The principal homological-error limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds timing hardware information—an Apple M3 Pro CPU with 11 cores—and clarifies the LP pseudocode's H-representations and output-equality constraint, consistent with the existing Equation 6. It removes v1's code-availability statement and repository address. This establishes loss of access information, not that the repository became unavailable.

R1.justification: v3 adds references on persistence landscapes, persistence images, persistent Laplacians, Mapper, neural-network topology, and Reeb spaces. Section 2.2 newly explains how its equivalence relation differs from a Reeb space. The central positioning relative to persistent homology and prior polyhedral research remains.

P1.justification: The title, affiliation, terminology, and numerous sentences are edited, while the main narrative and section sequence remain recognizable. The numerical-method subsections are consolidated, LP pseudocode moves to Appendix C.1, and the impact and code-availability sections disappear.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, substantially reflowing text, equations, tables, and figures. Figure 1 gains a conceptual gluing diagram, Figure 2 changes uncertainty shading, and new Figures 6–7 are added. v1's Figures 6–7 are retained as v3's Figures 8–9.

improvement.justification: v3 improves conceptual precision by aligning the theoretical statements with the quotient computation and explaining the relative-homology connection and coarser decomposition in Appendices A.5 and B.5. The new occupancy and timing diagnostics help readers assess applicability and cost. The gains are tempered by occupancy providing only indirect evidence of manifold convexity, removal of the code-access statement, and retained relative-homology labels in some graphics. Overall, the revision provides a limited net improvement in clarity and assessability.
